$comment: Neutral guardrail-hook SSOT for this repo — the hooks half of Argo's cross-CLI setup (skills are skills-lock.json's half). One entry per behavior; `packages/argo-skills/bin/hooks-sync.mjs` projects them into each harness named in `agents` below: claude-code -> .claude/settings.json, codex -> .codex/hooks.json. Never hand-edit those generated blocks — edit here and run `bun run hooks:sync`. Commands are harness-neutral: bare `graphify` (on PATH) and `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/scripts/*` (no $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). The commands invoke this repo's scripts/ via git-toplevel; scaffold.mjs can copy this file AND those scripts into a consumer before projecting, but only opt-in (`--hooks`) since the guard imposes Argo's worktree discipline. Optional top-level `worktreeGuard.roots` re-scopes the worktree edit guard (default `["apps", "packages"]`) for a project whose code lives elsewhere. See AGENTS.md "Cross-CLI guardrail hooks".

hooks.$comment: Glob, not Read|Glob. The guard emits ~400 B of context per fire, and it fires on any file newer than the graph — so in a linked worktree, where the pre-commit `graphify update` is skipped and the graph is stale against everything, matching Read billed roughly every file a session opened. Glob is the verb the orientation rule is actually about (orient before you sweep), and keeping it there preserves the staleness warning, which inside a worktree is the only signal the graph is out of date at all.

Write only — Edit cannot create a file, so an edit is never a placement decision. Denies a NEW file loose at a module root, which root-files-check.mjs would fail the build on later, once imports already point at it (ADR-0021).
